overview.text: The Common (Daudin's) Bronzeback is a slender, harmless tree snake of South Asia.

identification.text: Long and slim with a pointed head, plain ruddy brown, with a bronze line down the back.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh and Nepal, and possibly Pakistan, Bhutan and Myanmar.

habitat.text: Many kinds of forest, and even gardens and parks in towns.

behaviour.text: Active by day and lives in trees; special belly scales help it climb steep, smooth surfaces.

diet.text: Geckos, garden lizards, frogs and small birds.

reproduction.text: Lays 6 to 8 eggs in April, in tree hollows and rotting plants.

recognise.text: Slender bronze-brown snake with a pointed head.
